claims.statement: The data plane is an Electron `utilityProcess` child that owns all periodic collection — the five-tool session scan, hardware sampling, the usage log and the desktop scan/plan/store — together with their timers, while the main process keeps only the window host, hotzone poll, bridge/IPC, plugin host, icon extraction, shortcut resolution and launching; the child is assembled by `createDataplaneKernel`, which reuses the same service classes and injectable dependency seams as the in-process `createKernel`.

ADR-0005 derives two structural red lines from the mouse-stutter root cause — the window-host thread must never hold a system-level input hook (click-through is used without `forward`), and periodic collection must not run on the main-process event loop — because a forwarded mouse hook (`setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })`) made every system mouse event wait on the main-process thread while ~300 ms/s of blocking collection ran on that same thread.

The fix is backed by real-machine measurement from a 50 ms event-loop heartbeat probe over 140 s: before the move there were 139 stalls ≥150 ms with p99/max gaps of 367/2302 ms and main-process CPU at 35.29% of one core; after it there were 0 such stalls, max 68 ms, 1.82% main-process CPU, and the collection load visibly migrated into the utility child (0.07% → 3.78%).

`worker_threads` was rejected as the isolation mechanism because a SQLite `busy_timeout` stall or a `koffi` crash would then kill the panel together with the worker, whereas a separate utilityProcess lets the host detect the exit and restart it by backoff.

`PanelDataPort` is the single seam the bridge layer knows and it has two interchangeable implementations — `LocalPanelDataService` (in-process, direct service calls, real `refresh()`) for the offline kernel and contract tests, and `DataplaneService` (production) whose `refresh()` is a no-op because the child self-drives sampling and whose reads are plain field reads of the cached snapshot, so no production read path can block the main-process event loop.

Because no Electron API exists in the child, `DataplaneInit` injects the values only the main process can resolve: `roots` (user desktop plus public desktop, the only way to see an OneDrive redirection), `storeFile` (`userData/layout.json`), `docMaxRows` (`config.desktop.docMaxRows`) and `usageDir` (`userData/usage`, already migrated by the main process).

Both sides share one discriminated message union of exactly seven types — `init`, `ready`, `snapshot`, `resolve-shortcuts`, `shortcuts`, `req`, `res` — carried by `utilityProcess` `postMessage` and therefore by structured clone; the child entry is inert when `parentPort` is absent, ignores a repeated `init` so services and timers cannot be registered twice, and posts `ready` only after `ctx.start()` resolves.

A `DataplaneSnapshot` carries exactly four sections — `clock`, `sessions`, `hardware`, `desktop` — and deliberately excludes `weather`, `layout`, `settings` and `plugins`, which stay main-process properties and are merged into `PanelSnapshot` by `BridgeService.snapshot()`.

The child's cadence comes from `createDataplaneKernel`'s timers: a 1000 ms tick that runs `sessions.refresh()`, `desktop.refresh()` and then `onSnapshot(dataplaneSnapshot(ctx))`, a separate 1000 ms hardware sample timer, a 2000 ms usage-collect timer and an hourly usage prune; every interval has a `0`-disables switch so offline tests drive the same services manually.

`ready` is not a tick: it is posted right after `ctx.start()` and assembled from freshly constructed services, so the boot snapshot already carries the desktop section (the desktop service scans from its constructor) while `sessions` is still empty and the hardware block is still the zeroed initial state — which is what makes the readiness gate useful, since the dock is placed from `desktop.plan` and the first tick fills sessions and history.

The host handles `ready` and `snapshot` identically: it stores the snapshot as `latest` (the source of every read), resets the restart-attempt counter to 0, resolves `whenReady`, prewarms icons for desktop items whose `iconKey` still needs work, and emits the internal `dataplane/snapshot` event.

`dataplane/snapshot` is an internal cordis event declared only in the `Events` augmentation and not part of `BridgeEvents` or `FORWARDED_EVENTS`, so it can never reach the renderer; the indirection exists because `bridge` is not yet registered while the port implementation it injects is constructed, and `BridgeService` subscribes in its own constructor to push `panel/changed` on each arrival.

`ProxyShortcutResolver` keeps lnk-target resolution off the child's critical path: `resolve()` is synchronous, returns `null` on a cache miss, batches unanswered paths into one message per flush via `setImmediate`, uses an inflight set so an unanswered path is never asked twice, and caches every delivered answer including `null`; a miss therefore costs one tick of accuracy in recommendation ordering and converges on the next 1 Hz re-plan.

The main process memoizes shortcut targets in its own path-keyed map and answers repeats from there, so `electronShortcutTarget` (i.e. `shell.readShortcutLink`) runs at most once per path for the process lifetime — the memoization that also removed the previously uncached per-tick `readShortcutLink` calls from desktop plan scoring.

Icon extraction and launching stay in the main process: the child's desktop deps use `extractIcon: null` (so it scans and plans with no icon cache) and an `open` that throws `desktop/launch 由面板主进程执行`, while the main process prewarms `IconCache` from snapshot items and `launch()` validates the path against its own copy of the latest item pool before `shell.openPath`, which is why `desktop/launch` is deliberately not a data-plane method.

The write RPC path is exactly two methods — `desktop/move` and `desktop/reset-layout` — sent as `{ type: 'req', id, method, payload }` with a monotonically increasing id tracked in a pending-resolver map; the child executes its own `DesktopService.move`/`resetLayout` (item-pool and anchor validation, tmp-file-plus-rename store write, immediate re-plan) so the next snapshot already carries the new plan.

RPC failures arrive in two registers and there is no per-request timeout: a call rejects only when the child is absent at call time (`数据面子进程不在场`) or when the child exits (all pending rejected with `数据面子进程退出，请求失败`), the child answers `ok: false` for a thrown error, an unknown method, or a request received before `init` (`数据面尚未初始化`), and a business refusal comes back as a resolved result `{ ok: false, error }`; a child that is alive but wedged leaves the promise pending indefinitely.

Crash policy lives in `onExit`: it returns early when the service is `stopped`, drops the child reference, rejects every pending RPC, logs `{ type: 'dataplane-exit', code }`, and respawns after `Math.min(30_000, 1000 * 2 ** restartAttempt)` (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, then 30 s), incrementing the attempt counter that any `ready`/`snapshot` message resets to 0; cordis `dispose` instead sets `stopped`, clears a pending restart timer and kills the child.

A restart reuses the same `init` bundle, so the on-disk layout store, usage log and session scan converge in the new child, while the hardware history ring lives only in child memory and restarts empty, leaving a visible discontinuity in the 300-point series — an accepted display-only degradation in ADR-0005.

Before the first snapshot every read falls back to a placeholder rather than an error: `clock()` is synthesized locally from `new Date()`, `sessions()` is `[]`, `hardware()` is zeroed gauges `{ cpu: 0, memory: 0, memory_gb: '-- GB/-- GB' }` with empty history arrays, and `desktop()` is `{ fingerprint: '', items: [], plan: { dock: [], docs: [] } }`, so an empty item pool reaches icon prewarm and `desktop/launch`.

After the child exits, `latest` is never cleared: reads keep serving the pre-crash snapshot (stale, not empty) while the pushed `panel/changed` stream stops until the new child's first snapshot, and because `launch` validates against that cached item pool, a desktop item that appeared only after the crash is not launchable until a fresh snapshot arrives — the asymmetry of degraded reads versus frozen pushes.

The first-snapshot readiness gate is `DataplaneService.whenReady`: it resolves on the child's first `ready`/`snapshot` message or after `DEFAULT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` ms with a `dataplane-ready-timeout` log entry, and `bootPanel()` awaits it before creating the panel window; a timeout therefore only means the panel boots on an empty data plane and catches up on the first later snapshot, and the promise never re-arms after a crash.

The host's operational surface is a single evidence log plus child identity: the injected `log` callback records `dataplane-spawn` with `{ pid, reason }` where reason is `'boot'` or `'restart'`, `dataplane-exit` with the code, and `dataplane-ready-timeout`; the fork passes `serviceName: 'deck-dataplane'` and `stdio: 'inherit'`, so the child's own `deck-sessions:`/`deck-desktop:`/`deck-usage:` warnings surface in the parent's stream.

Offline coverage of the data plane is split: `tests/dataplane-kernel.spec.ts` assembles `createDataplaneKernel` in-process with fake sources and 10 ms timers, asserting the four snapshot sections and that `desktop/move` lands on disk and appears as a `placed` dock entry ahead of its anchor in the next snapshot; `tests/dataplane-protocol.spec.ts` pins the resolver's batching, same-round and in-flight de-duplication and null-caching; the child entry's `parentPort` glue and the Electron-only host are not unit-tested and are covered by the real-machine acceptance battery plus the evidence log.

The page's predecessor is retired history: the Python `server.py` data service, its watchdog and the Wallpaper Engine deployment chain were retired on 2026-09-29 (工单11), and the former path is preserved only as the retired term «数据服务» in the domain vocabulary.

Change-safety rules follow from the boundary: new periodic collection belongs inside `createDataplaneKernel` (never back on the main-process event loop), Electron-only capabilities must be reached through message types or `DataplaneInit` fields, a new read becomes a `DataplaneSnapshot` section merged in the main process, a new write becomes a `DataplaneMethod` with a child branch, `dataplane/snapshot` must stay out of `BridgeEvents`, snapshot and payload types must remain structured-clone-plain, and `latest` must not be cleared on exit without deliberately changing post-crash behaviour from stale to empty.
